the plasma treatment of fibers is a very promising approach to improve the composite strength of endless fiber-reinforced injection molded parts.
plasma pretreatment is a promising method to enhance the fiber-matrix adhesion and the resulting bond strength of the fiber reinforced composite, which was shown for the first time in this work.
the atmospheric pressure plasma treatment of the glass fibers leads to a significant improvement of the bond strength of fiber and matrix.

the investigation of the influence of plasma treatment on the fiber-matrix adhesion in endless fiber-reinforced injection molded parts.
the direct integration of endless fibers in injection-molded components.
the direct impregnating of fibers in the injection process and the improvement of the composite behavior by the surface modification of the fibers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a pretreatment of the glass fiber by plasma is necessary to achieve an optimal composite strength of the endless fibers in injection molding.
the plasma pretreatment of the glass fibers has an important effect on fiber/matrix adhesion and thus on the mechanical strength.
the atmospheric pressure plasma treatment of glass fibers has a positive effect on the composite strength of endless fiber-reinforced injection molded components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma pretreatment of the fiber surface has a significant effect on the composite strength.
the plasma treatment of glass fibers is a promising method to improve the bond strength and to increase the mechanical properties of the composite.
plasma treatment of glass fibers is an effective method to improve the bond strength of glass fibers in the direct impregnated injection molded components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma parameters have a significant influence on the bond strength of glass fibers and the matrix.
the plasma treatment of the glass fiber surface leads to a higher bond strength and a better composite behavior of endless glass fibers in the injection molded component.
the adhesion of the glass fibers can be improved by plasma pretreatment, which is a prerequisite to produce high-strength composites.
